subject: Imposing consistency and sparsity in Transition matrix

messages.author: 9be5ae75921aca4a
messages.subject: Imposing consistency and sparsity in Transition matrix
parts:
I am dealing with a a transition matrix theta in my HMM model. I wish to enforce consistency in the chain (i.e. stays in the same state for a while before switching) and sparsity so that it doesn't switch to many other states. The first is more important than the latter.

So for instance if theta is declared as:
simplex[K] theta[K];  // transit probs

Is there a way to put the lower bound that theta[k][k]>0.9 for all k?

Thanks,
Sachin

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Imposing consistency and sparsity in Transition matrix
parts:
Not unless you construct the simplex from some latent space where
you can impose the constraint exactly.  But for this purpose a soft
constraint will just work as well, which is easily implemented by adding
a Dirichlet prior to each simplex with the kth hyperparameter significantly
larger than the rest.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Imposing consistency and sparsity in Transition matrix
parts:
In general, we don't recommend hard constraints.
Instead we prefer to let the data determine what the values
should be. The problem you'll run into with hard constraints
is that the data may not be consistent with them and you'll
be trying to estimate parameters right up against boundaries,
which is problematic both statistically and computationally.

You can, if you really want to, set the Dirichlet prior to
be high enough to guarantee that the value is greater than 0.9,
because you can exploit the conjugacy to figure out what the
parameter needs to be.

If you really insist on doing what you suggest, then you
either need to do what Michael says and reparameterize, or
you need to do something like the following

parameters {
simplex[K] theta_raw;

transformed parameters {
simplex[K] theta;
theta <- 0.1 * theta_raw;
theta[k] <- theta[k] + 0.9;

Then theta will have theta[k] > 0.9. But it's going to be very
poorly behaved if the data's not consistent with theta[k] > 0.9.

- Bob
